question: Hand preference before 12 months of age is the single most sensitive early sign of infantile hemiplegia.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. A child should NOT show a consistent hand preference before 18 months — both hands are used equally in normal development. When a parent or examiner notices that a child always uses one hand and avoids the other before 12 months, it strongly suggests a unilateral upper motor neurone deficit (infantile hemiplegia). This sign should trigger neurological evaluation and MRI brain.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Handedness normally develops only after 18 months to 2 years of age. A strong hand preference before 12 months — always reaching with one hand, never using the other — is abnormal and the earliest detectable sign of infantile hemiplegia (hemiplegic CP). The affected hand is used less because the corticospinal tract from the ipsilateral hemisphere is damaged, making this a key clinical red flag for early referral.
